title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents to develop and implement integrated, inclusive, and transformative care economy agendas that promote inclusive decent work opportunities

description.narrative: Egypt’s care economy faces major structural gaps, including limited access to quality care services, a disproportionate burden of unpaid care work on women, and high informality with weak labour protection for care workers such as domestic and childcare workers. Persons with disabilities also encounter persistent barriers to labour market inclusion. These challenges constrain women’s labour force participation, limit decent job creation in the care sector, and hinder progress toward gender equality and inclusive economic growth. Addressing these gaps requires strengthening national capacities to design and implement integrated, gender-responsive and inclusive care policies aligned with international labour standards and supported by social dialogue. Priorities include developing evidence-based diagnostics and costing to inform policy and investment; advancing legal and institutional frameworks for domestic workers; and establishing a comprehensive childcare policy that expands access to quality services while ensuring decent work for childcare workers. Efforts also promote inclusive employment for persons with disabilities, including through private sector engagement and the establishment of a Business Disability Network. Primary beneficiaries include women and men in paid and unpaid care work, as well as persons with disabilities seeking decent employment. Indirect beneficiaries include families—especially women—who benefit from improved access to affordable, quality care services, enabling greater labour market participation. Government institutions and social partners benefit from strengthened capacities in care policy and labour market governance. Coordination with development partners and UN agencies supports policy coherence, knowledge sharing, and resource mobilization..
